newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier says 30 jets need repairs.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier says 30 jets need repairs.

text.p: Bombardier Inc said on Friday that 30 of 121 of its 50-seat Canadair Regional Jets (CRJs) inspected for cracks in their pressure bulkhead frames will require repairs.

Those repairs are expected to be completed in the next few day, Catherine Chase, spokeswoman for Bombardier's Canadair unit, told Reuters. All of the 166 CRJs delivered to customers will be inspected under a Transport Canada air worthiness order issued (on) Thursday.
Chase said repair kits consisting of sheet metal and fasteners and Canadair technicians were being dispatched to the seven North American and European airlines affected.
"They will begin these repairs this evening," she said.
Those airlines include Air Canada, SkyWest Airlines and Comair Holdings Inc.
The aircraft were being in inspected for possible fatigue cracks in the pressure bulkhead frame at the forward end of the their fuselage wing box cutout.
The inspections were ordered by Transport Canada in an emergency airworthiness directive that became effective on Thursday.
Bombardier shares rose by 1.15 in Toronto to 31.00 on 1.16 million shares by the end of Friday's session, recovering the 1.15 lost late Thursday.
